Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is safe for the narrow gate of running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. The top-level scope contains only standard variable assignments (pkgname, pkgver, dependencies, etc.) with no command substitution, no `eval`, no encoded payloads, and no other executable code beyond simple string expansions. There is no `pkgver()` function that could execute arbitrary logic during sourcing. The `source` array fetches from the package's own upstream repository (`git+https://github.com/potassco/clingo#tag=v${pkgver}`), which is standard practice for VCS sources. The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` is expected and correct for a git VCS source. The `build()` and `package()` functions would not execute during these commands, so their contents are out of scope for this gate.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard VCS PKGBUILD, safe for sourcing and source fetching.</summary>
</security_assessment>
